LLM guardrails are systems designed to protect
deployed LLMs by evaluating user input - detect-        2.2   Threat Model
ing malicious content such as prompt injections         We consider two threat models based on the level
and jailbreaks, and restrict undesired content gen-     of access to the LLM guardrails. Black-box targets
erated by LLMs to within predefined boundaries.         are systems that only provide a classification label
Guardrails can leverage a range of techniques that      or block the request when a malicious prompt is de-
attempt to govern behavior and output and prevent       tected. We assume that access to these targets can
malicious use by adversaries (Dong et al., 2024).       be attained via API endpoints without rate limits
                                                        or query restrictions. White-box targets, provide
                                                        additional information such as confidence scores
                                                        or logits, allowing attackers to carry out more ef-
                                                        fective attacks. White-box targets are accessed
                                                        by downloading open-source models used by the
                                                        target, either identified through documentation or
                                                        publicly available information. The attackers goal
                                                        across both threat models is to successfully evade

        Numbers                       Mapping letters to certain numbers.                  H3110
        Homoglyph                     Replacing characters with homoglyphs.                Hello
        Zero Width                    Inserting non-printing characters (\u200B).           He ll o
        Diacritics                    Replacing vowels with its diacritical equivalent.    hèllö
        Spaces                        Adding spaces between each letter in the text.       Hello
        Underline Accent Marks        Underlines the text using Unicode.                   Hello
        Upside Down Text              Text is flipped upside down.                         Hello
        Full Width Text               Characters are made full-width.                      Hello
        Bidirectional Text            Text is flipped right to left.                       olleH
        Deletion Characters           Characters are randomly removed.                     Hlo
        Emoji Smuggling               Text is embedded in emoji variation selectors.
        Unicode Tag Smuggling         Text is embedded within Unicode tags.

 Evasion Attack                              Description
 Bert-Attack (Li et al., 2020)               Masked tokens are added to the prompt and a BERT model
                                             to generate perturbations.
 BAE (Garg and Ramakrishnan, 2020)           Contextual perturbations from a BERT-MLM masked model
                                             by replacing and inserting masked tokens in the prompt.
 Deep Word Bug (Gao et al., 2018)            Character-level transformations are applied to the highest-
                                             ranked tokens to minimize distance of the perturbation.
 Alzantot (Alzantot et al., 2018)            Population-based optimization via genetic algorithms (GA).
                                             Replaces words with semantically similar counterparts.
 TextFooler (Jin et al., 2020)               Words with the highest importance ranking are replaced with
                                             suitable replacement words with similar semantic meaning.
 PWWS (Ren et al., 2019)                     Probability Weighted Word Salience (PWWS) ranks word
                                             importance using word saliency and classification probability.
 Pruthi (Pruthi et al., 2019)                Generates perturbations in the form of adversarial spelling
                                             mistakes via removing or swapping characters.
 TextBugger (Li et al., 2019)                Generates utility-preserving adversarial text against black-
                                             box and white-box classification systems.

6     Discussion
                                                          6.3    Guardrails and LLM Input Differences
6.1    Guardrail Evasion Success
                                                          The relationship between guardrails and LLMs re-
Character injection techniques have demonstrated          veal interesting differences in how they handle in-
to be highly effective while requiring minimal            puts. LLM Guardrails can be trained on entirely dif-
effort from adversaries. Interestingly, smug-             ferent datasets than the underlying LLM, resulting
gling techniques such as emoji, and unicode tags          in their inability to detect certain character injec-
emerged as effective injections, while other tech-        tion techniques that the LLM itself can understand.
niques varied in success suggesting that target LLM       As shown in Section 5.1, character injection tech-
guardrails can differ in susceptibility to this type of   niques can completely evade guardrail detection.
evasion. This points to weaknesses in the underly-        This poses a risk because inputs that bypass the
ing model architecture or training process. The ef-       guardrails may still be properly interpreted by the
fectiveness of these attacks likely varies depending      LLM (Claburn, 2024). In addition to differences
on the training data each model has been exposed          in training data, guardrails may also have inher-
to, emphasizing the differences in learned behav-         ent design differences—such as limited input size
ior and susceptibility across different targets (Wei      and token support—that can be exploited to fur-
et al., 2025). Models trained on diverse datasets or      ther evade classification (Wei et al., 2025). These
those with better generalized understanding are typ-      limitations highlight a critical weakness in current
ically more resistant, while others remain vulnera-       guardrail implementations and demonstrate a fur-
ble due to the specific content they’ve encountered       ther need to understand how inputs could be crafted
during training.                                          to intentionally bypass guardrails while remaining
